items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Switch 2 Deep Look
Final Fantasy XIV Online Updated On Switch 2, Here Are The Full Patch Notes
items.content:
Square Enix already gave us a handy heads up that it would address some loading issues with Final Fantasy XIV Online for the Switch 2.

Now, the update is live, but it brings a host of other improvements and fixes along with it, several of which are specifically for Nintendo's console. The loading is the highlight, of course, but we've also got improvements to touch screen functionality and more.

So make sure you update the game to the latest version manually if it doesn't do it automatically (and it really should). For now, here's a look at the full patch notes:

■ Optimised processing to speed up data loading to reduce the time of screen transitions within duties. (Nintendo Switch™ 2 version only) ■ The following issues have been addressed: - Upon completing the Allied Society Quest “Hero's Day Off,” a message notifying that your reputation had advanced to “Allied” would not appear. - In the Occult Crescent: North Horn, the quest "In the Shadow of the Tower" would display the quest completed icon above the NPC even if the objective had not been completed. - In the following duties, if a player logged out while incapacitated and then logged back in more than 10 minutes later, they could return to the duty despite having been expelled. - The Occult Crescent: South Horn - Forked Tower: Blood - The Occult Crescent: North Horn - Forked Tower: Magic - The Occult Crescent: North Horn - The Forked Tower: Magic (Extreme) - The Forbidden Land, Eureka Hydatos - The Baldesion Arsenal - In the Occult Crescent, when a player had multiple damage-nullifying buffs from the following phantom actions, receiving damage would not only consume the buff of the corresponding damage type, but other damage-nullifying buffs as well. Shirahadori / Image / Occult Blink - In the Occult Crescent: North Horn critical encounter “Dark Artistry,” the visual effect of the enemy action “Dark Flare” appeared narrower than the actual attack. - In the Occult Crescent: North Horn critical encounter “Accept No Imitators,” no sound effect was played when the visual indicator for the boss action “Spinebreaking Stampede” was displayed. - In the Occult Crescent: North Horn FATE “Eye to Eye,” certain visual effects from the boss actions ”Cold Stare” and “Sinister Sight” were displayed for players who were not participating in the FATE. - In the Occult Crescent: North Horn, stepping onto the circles to travel to specific locations could cause players to become stuck in the ground or midair and prevent movement. - The animations/visual effects for the following phantom actions were not displayed properly in the Occult Crescent. Occult Aero III / Occult Holy / Chaos Drive / Punishing Ray / Drain Touch / Step Forth - Visual effects were not depicted properly at certain camera angles for the following weapons when they were drawn. Phantom Spear Occultum / Phantom Cane Occultum / Phantom Index Occultum / Phantom Codex Occultum / Phantom Revolver Occultum / Phantom Degen Occultum - When Tradewinds Gaskins were equipped along with certain foot gear on the following races/genders, graphics around the waist were displayed incorrectly: Midlander Male / Highlander Male / Elezen Male / Miqo'te Male / Au Ra Male / Viera Male - When Vana'dielian Tights of Healing were equipped on the following races/genders, the graphics of the left leg were displayed incorrectly when an idle animation entered a specific pose: Midlander Female / Highlander Female / Elezen Female / Viera Female - The keybind and log filter settings saved via Configuration Sharing were stored under "Miscellaneous Data" instead of "Character Configuration." - Touch screen input was not recognised as player input during duties, causing players using only touch screen controls to be treated as inactive and forcibly removed from duties after a certain period of time. (Nintendo Switch™ 2 version only) - In the Gold Saucer GATE "Air Force One", shots fired via touch screen controls were launched toward the previous reticle position rather than the location touched. (Nintendo Switch™ 2 version only) - Duty Recorder replay data did not play back correctly when a chapter was selected while the replay was paused. (Nintendo Switch™ 2 version only)

We're still busy tinkering away at our review for Final Fantasy XIV Online, so if you're on the fence about this one, then be sure to check it out when it's live.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV launches a free trial on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: The most popular MMORPG finally arrives to Nintendo SWitch 2, and you can try it for free.
items.content:
The gates to Eorzea have officially opened on Nintendo Switch 2, and this time, you don't need to buy a ticket. Square Enix has launched the Final Fantasy XIV Free Trial on the new console, giving curious adventurers the chance to experience one of the world's most successful MMORPGs without paying a subscription or worrying about a time limit.

Calling it a "trial" almost feels misleading. Rather than offering a brief taste of the game, the free version includes the entirety of A Realm Reborn and the first three expansions— Heavensward , Stormblood , and Shadowbringers . New players can journey through an enormous story spanning hundreds of quests, challenge iconic bosses, clear dungeons and raids, and experiment with every available combat, crafting, and gathering job up to level 80. It's enough content to keep most RPG fans occupied for months.

One of Final Fantasy XIV's biggest strengths is its flexibility. A single character can learn every class in the game, allowing players to swap between roles whenever they like instead of creating multiple characters. Whether you prefer charging into battle as a tank, keeping allies alive as a healer, dealing massive damage, or taking a break to become Eorzea's finest blacksmith or fisherman, the Free Trial lets you experience nearly every side of the game.

As generous as it is, the trial isn't completely unrestricted. Free accounts cannot use the Market Board, trade items with other players, create parties or Free Companies, send direct messages, or participate in PvP modes. There's also a cap of 300,000 gil, ensuring the trial remains focused on exploration and story rather than the game's player-driven economy.

There's one important detail for newcomers: the Free Trial is only available for new service accounts. Once an account purchases the full game, it permanently transitions to the standard version, which requires a monthly subscription after the included game time expires. For that reason, players may want to squeeze every last dungeon, raid, and side quest out of the trial before making the jump.

Switch 2 owners should also make sure they have plenty of room to spare. Final Fantasy XIV requires around 117 GB of free storage, making it one of the largest downloads currently available on Nintendo's latest console. On the bright side, there's no need for a Nintendo Switch Online membership to play, so once the game is installed, the only thing standing between you and your next adventure is deciding which job to level first.

For anyone who's been waiting for the right moment to see what all the excitement is about, this might be it. With four complete chapters of the saga available at no cost, the Switch 2 Free Trial offers an adventure that's less of a demo and more of a full-blown fantasy epic. items.title: Final Fantasy XIV on Switch 2 is Better Than Anyone Expected
items.summary: Final Fantasy XIV is shaping up to be one of the Switch 2's most technically ambitious ports, with Square Enix targeting stable performance while bringing the full MMORPG experience to Nintendo's latest hybrid console.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV is shaping up to be one of the Switch 2's most technically ambitious ports, with Square Enix targeting stable performance while bringing the full MMORPG experience to Nintendo's latest hybrid console.

When Final Fantasy XIV was first announced for Nintendo Switch 2, skepticism was understandable. This is, after all, an MMORPG that has been evolving continuously for more than a decade. It spans multiple expansions, supports hundreds of players in shared social spaces, features massive raids, sprawling cities, and some of the busiest online hubs in gaming.

Translating all of that to a handheld system seemed like an enormous technical challenge. But it's clear that Square Enix seems to be taking on the task very seriously based on our early impressions of the game so far today at launch.

Producer and director Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P) has confirmed that the team has prioritized consistent performance over raw frame rate, targeting a stable 30 FPS throughout the majority of gameplay . Rather than chasing higher numbers, the focus has been on maintaining smooth combat and reliable frame pacing during the content players spend most of their time enjoying things like main scenario quests, dungeons, trials, raids, crafting, gathering, and exploration.

"I want to be honest with you: we are working really hard on the optimisation. We are striving to get the best performance. I think with the towns, you may see a lower framerate, only because there are so many players that are rendered on the screen.

The Nintendo Switch 2 is a wonderful console, and I think you can choose the way you want to play. You are more free to choose which mode to play in, so I hope that players will find the way to play that is most suited for themselves."

- Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P), game director, during a press conference

Cities like Limsa Lominsa regularly fill with hundreds of player characters showing off mounts, glamour sets, minions, and particle-heavy abilities. Even on significantly more powerful hardware, those areas have historically been among the game's toughest rendering scenarios. Square Enix has been transparent that these locations are where Switch 2 players are most likely to see performance fluctuate, but the team says it has spent considerable time optimizing the experience leading up to launch.

From the time I've spent with the game so far, you can definitely feel the impact. But since these are social gathering areas or just dialogue- and menu-heavy environments, it's not really a big detractor from gameplay. When you're outside of the city doing quests or in an instance, it's been very smooth so far.

I picked up playing with my level 30 Gladiator I abandoned a few years ago on PC, so it's been a little bit of a learning curve so far. Fortunately, if you really want to, you don't have to play in handheld mode or using a controller since there's mouse support on Switch 2, including both USB options and the Joy-Con's mouse mode.

"As everyone already knows, the Nintendo Switch 2 is an amazing piece of hardware. If you place it in the dock, you can play in TV mode. If you use it in Portable mode, you can carry it and play it at your leisure. For example, when challenging a high-difficulty Raid, you can play on TV while connecting a mouse and keyboard, and then you can craft and gather while in Portable mode. I feel like this will enable a play style that is unique to Nintendo Switch 2.

Following the announcement at the keynote speech, I also saw some voices on social media asking, 'Is it going to be alright spec-wise?', but we are thoroughly optimizing it. There are no performance issues at all during actual content. It's much more hectic when you're in a town with a lot of characters, though I think it should run stably around 30 frames there as well. The performance is better in the actual content, so I think it should be okay, and you should not worry."

- Naoki Yoshida (Yoshi-P), game director, in an interview with Famitsu reported by RPGSite

Unlike many MMORPG adaptations, this isn't a separate handheld version with isolated servers or reduced functionality. Switch 2 players log into the same persistent world as everyone else across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. Every expansion, every raid, every social space, every seasonal event, and every update arrives together, allowing players to seamlessly continue their existing characters wherever they choose to play in both handheld and docked modes.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Switch 2 Launch Is a Surprise Success With One Huge Catch
items.summary: Performance impresses on Switch 2, even as subscription issues frustrate
items.content:
Listen Thread 2 Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Willa Rowe Published Aug 4, 2026, 10:33 AM EDT News Performance impresses on Switch 2, even as subscription issues frustrate

Final Fantasy 14 could finally introduce a controversial feature to welcome new players Pokémon studio's new game arrives on Xbox Game Pass today Rust's major August update is concerning for solo players Final Fantasy 14's Switch 2 launch is going better than expected, mostly Final Fantasy 14 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Warriors of Light can finally explore Eorzea on the Nintendo Switch 2 . On Tuesday, Aug. 4, Square Enix finally released Final Fantasy 14 on the hybrid console-handheld. For the most part, players report that things are going pretty well!

This marks the beginning of what Square Enix is calling a one-month early access period for Final Fantasy 14 on Switch 2. During this time, players can enjoy everything the critically acclaimed MMORPG has to offer just as they would on any other platform. Square Enix will not enforce the game's subscription requirement during the first month on Switch 2. Regardless of whether you are a new or returning player, you can enjoy Final Fantasy 14 on Switch 2 entirely for free during the early access period.

There is a caveat to this good news. When the early access period does end, subscriptions will be required and there's a special Nintendo tax . Typically, Warriors of Light pay for a single subscription that works for all platforms the MMO is available on. The Switch 2 version of Final Fantasy 14 , however, will require its own subscription, even for those who have active subscriptions already.

To mitigate the extra cost, Square Enix is offering Switch 2 subscriptions at half price for players with existing subscriptions. Furthermore, players do not need a Nintendo Switch Online subscription to play the online game. The complete edition of Final Fantasy 14 , which includes all currently released expansions, is also on sale for a limited time at a discount of 30%. Though if you are just curious to try the MMO, start by downloading the free trial. Once you purchase the game in any way, you can't use the free trial without creating a new account entirely.

Even with all the extra hoops to jump through on Switch 2, players are reporting that the game is running very smoothly. Some Warriors of Light, eager to test out just how much the console can handle, went directly to the Limsa Lominsa Aetheryte Plaza, one of the consistently busiest locations in the game. In handheld mode, the Switch 2 was able to perform admirably in this rendering gauntlet. If performance was players' biggest worry before the Switch 2 release, today's launch has assuaged those concerns. Most reactions on social media are just sharing their awe that the game runs as well as it does.

That isn't to say the launch has been without hiccups. Some players are posting excessively long download times. While the game's 117 GB is nothing to sneeze at, waiting over a dozen hours for the download to complete seems excessive. Of course, this could be caused by individual network issues and not a platform problem. The biggest issue players are facing is getting the game to work with existing accounts.

There are already a couple posts on the Final Fantasy 14 subreddit asking for help troubleshooting the complex setup process on Switch 2. Hopefully these are just growing pains of launching the MMO on a new platform and Square Enix will sort it out soon enough. The game is technically still in an early access period on Switch 2. Players can follow a detailed guide on how to set up the game on Switch 2 on the Final Fantasy 14 blog .

Overall, feedback has been resoundingly positive for the Switch 2 launch. At the very least, it gives curious players who have never tried the beloved MMO a perfect reason to finally see what all the fuss is about before the Evercold expansion is released in January.

items.title: PSA: Final Fantasy 14 Is Out Now On Nintendo Switch 2 But You Don't Have To Buy It To Play
items.summary: Hope you have that meme memorized because it's relevant again; something something free trial something something
items.content:
By now, if you’re a Final Fantasy XIV player, you’re sick of the copypasta that starts, “ Have you heard of the critically acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV ? ” But loathe as I am to invoke a meme that’s long, long been run into the ground…it’s actually relevant again. Final Fantasy XIV is out on the Nintendo Switch 2 today. And if you’re one of the folks interested in trying the critically acclaimed MMORPG on the go, you may be tempted to buy one of the versions that’s now on sale at 30 percent off.

But you shouldn’t. Because, as the meme is so fond of reminding us, there’s a free trial available . And over the years, as the game has grown through expansions, the free trial expanded too. Now, instead of just getting A Realm Reborn and Heavensward and being able to play up to level 60, you get access to Stormblood and Shadowbringers too, bringing the character level cap up to 80. The freebies also include access to all the job classes released with the expansions: Machinist, Astrologian, Dancer, Dark Knight, Red Mage, Gunbreaker, and Samurai.

After you’ve reached the end of Shadowbringers , the next purchase step is the Final Fantasy XIV Complete Edition which includes the latest expansions, Endwalker and Dawntrail . Once you purchase any license for the game, you get 30 days of subscription time for free before you’ll be forced to kick out money for a monthly subscription. Players who have an active subscription on another platform will have to buy a new one (at half price) for the Switch 2, and a separate license. But one perk of playing FFXIV on the Nintendo Switch 2 (and the Playstation 5 for that matter) is that you don’t need to pay for an additional online subscription to play like you do on Xbox .

The free trial does come with certain restrictions. For example, chat commands are limited, you won’t have access to everything in the online store, you’ll be allowed a maximum of 300,000 gil (in-game currency), and a big one— you won’t be able to create your own party but you can be invited to a party or join one in the dungeon queue. Check out the full list of what’s allowed and what’s not here to plan you free-trial trip through Eorzea accordingly.

Patch 7.51 introduces the seventh installment of the ultimate raid series, Dancing Mad (Ultimate), as well as new custom deliveries featuring Tiisol Ja. And for our intrepid Disciples of the Hand and Land, new exploration awaits on Auxesia. * Additional features will be implemented in future updates:
  • The Occult Crescent: North Horn, Weapon Enhancement Quests - Phantom Weapons, Inconceivably Further Hildibrand Adventures sidequests, and Allied Society capstone sidequests are scheduled to release in Patch 7.55.
